text:
cheng: Heads-up — saw a ~30% throughput drop on canary after the nf4/fp4 mixed rollout at ~06:10 UTC. Memory on one host jumped and triggered OOM-kill for the inference worker. Logs attached below.

alex: ugh, saw the alert too. Was this the canary that flipped the new sampling-window batching heuristic?

cheng: yes — we enabled sampling_window_v2 that biases for longer prefixes to increase cache hits. Thought it would help throughput, not hurt.

maria: quick snapshot from profiling: kernel selection trace shows a lot more fallbacks to the slow fp4_slowpath kernel and increased host->gpu memcpy. Looks like the runtime decided kernel X (nf4_fast) wasn't compatible and switched to fp4_slowpath for longer sequences.

perf-bench: paste logs: 
```
[06:10:12] model: redwood-nf4-1  seq_len=1024 batch=8
[06:10:12] kernel_select: preferred=nf4_int8_fast candidate=fp4_slowpath reason=kv_misaligned
[06:10:12] batch_pack: sampling_window=64 -> microbatch 4->8
[06:10:13] memcpy: host_to_device 420MB (peak)
[06:10:14] latency p95 +40% throughput -30%
```

ida: "kv_misaligned" in the select path is suspicious — we've seen that when prefix alignment heuristics change and the KV cache memory layout doesn't match the expected packing for the nf4 kernels. Could be fragmentation.

ron: any chance calibration params for nf4/fp4 got mismatched? If quant scales or zero-points differ between canary and baseline we see fallback to slower packing and extra conversions.

cheng: we didn't change calibration in config, but the model artifact pushed yesterday had a new quant metadata file. I will diff that.

maria: attaching heapmap and kv allocation snapshot (short). Looks like many small KV slabs (64KB) instead of the large 1MB buckets we typically expect. The allocator's slab size decreased after sampling_window_v2 increased microbatching. Small slabs -> more host->device churn.

perf-bench: quick flame: majority of cycles now in memcpy and slow_gemm_fp4_slowpath. The nf4 optimized kernels are avoided because the runtime's compatibility check fails on stride/packing.

alex: action items: 1) flip sampling_window_v2 off in canary 2) force kernel selection telemetry for affected requests 3) capture exact model artifact and quant meta for failing hosts

maria: +1. Also we should run a packing-compatibility check in the onboarding pipeline to catch slab/packing mismatches earlier.

cheng: rolling back sampling_window_v2 now. pinging deploy-bot.

sre-bot: deploy request received for canary group: sampling_window_v2=false. Estimated completion 06:18 UTC.

perf-bench: while rollback is in flight, here's a quick repro command to generate same microbatch mix: 
```
# use stress-client with seq distribution skew
python tools/stress_client.py --model redwood-nf4-1 --rate 40 --seq-dist "long=0.6,mid=0.3,short=0.1" --microbatch-policy sampling_window_v2
```

ida: after rollback, we should run this and capture kernel_select traces: log lines to grep: "kernel_select:" and "kv_alloc:". Also dump allocator histogram at the same time.

cheng: rollback completed at 06:18, throughput back to baseline within ~2 minutes on most hosts. One host still had elevated memcpy, investigating.

ron: I diffed the quant meta files — the new model had a field "packed_stride=16" missing, so runtime treated the model as unpacked and selected the general (slower) fp4 path. That explains the fallbacks.

maria: oof. So two interacting causes: sampling_window_v2 increased slab churn and the model metadata omitted packed_stride -> combined led to kernel misroute + memory spike.

perf-bench: mitigation checklist: 
- add CI check for packed_stride in quant metadata
- make kernel_select log include model artifact version and quant fields
- add allocator telemetry to show slab distribution per host
- guard sampling_window_v2: only enable when allocator slab_histogram.mean > X

ida: also consider making kernel_select tolerant: if the preferred kernel would be a big perf win, try an on-the-fly repack path (costly but better than full fallback). Could be a stopgap for rollout.

alex: agree. For now let's: 1) push CI check 2) audit last 3 model artifacts for missing packed_stride 3) unpin canary on hosts with KV fragmentation.

cheng: I'll create a follow-up ticket with telemetry links and add owners for each mitigation. Ticket: INF-1723. Assigning to maria/ron/ida.

maria: FYI — perf regression writeup draft: short explanation, root cause (metadata + sampling_window), impact numbers, and mitigation steps. Will attach to ticket.

ron: long-term: we should unify quant metadata format and validate in model registry before deploy. Also consider embedding packing hints in the runtime image to avoid fragile metadata assumptions.

perf-bench: closing notes: this shows calibration/metadata errors can amplify when runtime batching heuristics change allocation patterns. Need stronger end-to-end guardrails.

cheng: thanks everyone — good catch. I'll follow up with logs and the ticket link once created. :thumbsup:
